judgment.notes: The commutator identities are instantiated on nonnegative powers in the complex representation. All factorial divisions and eigenvalue differences used are nonzero in C. The finite-dimensional basis criterion applies with exactly n independent vectors in dimension n (BG001). The two binomial upper arguments are integers at least r in their respective branches (BG002). There are no E/M applications.

S001 proves both identities with correct bases and induction steps. S002 obtains nonvanishing by applying x^i and proves independence using a polynomial in h that isolates each coefficient. Its cardinality/dimension argument gives a basis. S003 compares coefficients of y^(λ+1)v in that basis; every difference 2(λ+1−i) is nonzero, giving termination and all higher vanishing. Dividing by i! yields the stated generator formulas. S004 iterates them, handles both zero branches and r=0, and gives exactly the exported divided-power formulas and integral entries. The endpoint λ=0 is included.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
